`pybigwig_test.bw` is copied unmodified from pyBigWig's own test suite
(`pyBigWigTest/test.bw` in the `pyBigWig` PyPI package, MIT licensed).
Used as a real, independently-verifiable BigWig fixture for
`crates/formats/src/bigwig.rs` tests: ground truth for its contents was
captured via `pyBigWig.open(...)` directly (see
`crates/formats/src/bigwig.rs` test module for the exact expected
values). Two chromosomes: `1` (195471971bp) and `10` (130694993bp), a
handful of small intervals near the start of each.

`cram_no_reference.cram` is generated by this project's own
`make_cram_no_reference_fixture.py` (a real `pysam`-written CRAM file,
not copied from elsewhere). Used by `crates/formats/src/lib.rs`'s
`open_alignments` tests: one 4bp read (name `r1`, `4M`, `ACGT`,
mapping quality 40, 1-based alignment start 11) written with no
external reference configured, which makes htslib itself fall back to
embedding the reference in the CRAM (`embed_ref=2`) -- the case this
port's CRAM support (a default, empty `noodles_cram` reference
repository) is designed to handle. Not byte-reproducible across
regenerations (htslib embeds a non-deterministic field somewhere in
its own CRAM writer, same class of issue as gzip's own mtime header),
so don't regenerate it unless it's actually invalid -- the committed
bytes are the fixture.
